background.task:
All five acceptance criteria were exercised end-to-end against the running MockSite (`http://localhost:18080`) with the locally-built backend (dev mode, port 8282), and every branch of SKILL.md §4d was covered.

**AC3 — single-page acquisition: PASS.** Three product detail pages (`/ec/dp/B0A000001..3`) were visited with `goto` and each was exported with `htmlsnapshot export --file`, producing a 3-file corpus (~14 KB each) in `.test-sessions/20261015T0901431699046Z/corpus-small/`.

**AC1 — free WebMiner pipeline, small corpus: PASS.** `webminer all corpus-small` completed in ~5 s: encode (3 documents, 145 nodes, 180,977 bytes → CSV), SMILE KMeans (k=59 auto-detected, silhouette 0.6941), views. All three artifact classes exist: encoded dataset CSV **and** the views under `%TEMP%\webminer-pereg\…` (as documented), clustering results under `corpus-small-ml-output/kmeans-result/p20261017021812/` (3× `result.csv` + `clusteringInfo.txt`). The `webminer views <result-dir>` rebuild branch also works (3.6 s, views land in-tree next to the results). The same pipeline ran on the 8-page crawled corpus (478 nodes, k=65). This is confirmed as the correct branch — both corpora are far below the 1,000-page free-tier guidance.

**AC4 — bulk acquisition from known URLs: PASS (with a reliability incident).** An 8-URL seed file was fetched with `crawl --seed-file … --depth 0 --refresh` (8/8 OK in 9.9 s, titles confirmed). The documented staging step — crawling stores HTML in webdb — was completed with `webdb export` (8/8 `ok`, `.htm` files), and WebMiner consumed that directory unchanged, so the crawl → WebMiner handoff works. Mid-session the fetch layer wedged: every *fresh* fetch began failing with `PrivacyException`/status 1601 (13/24 in one crawl, then 4/6 reproducibly, then any new URL, even alone), while `goto`/`htmlsnapshot` stayed healthy. Only a full `stop` + backend restart restored fetching (all 6 previously-failing URLs then returned 200); the 8-URL crawl was re-verified 8/8 afterwards.

**AC5 — swarm acquisition: PASS (functionally), but the "high-throughput" premise did not hold.** `swarm create --display-mode HEADLESS` (2 contexts × 8 tabs) followed by `swarm query --seed-file … --sql @query.sql --refresh` submitted 8 jobs (batch id returned, all 8 completed in ~26 s) and a 24-URL batch (24/24 completed, 0 failed, 113 s). `swarm result <task-id>` returned correct X-SQL rows (title/price/rating/rating_count). However, on identical input the swarm path was ~3× slower than plain crawl for fresh fetches (8 URLs: ~26 s vs 9.9 s), and cached swarm tasks complete in ~10 ms — the per-task durations ramp in a near-perfect ~2.5 s stagger, i.e. fresh loads appear to execute one at a time despite 2 contexts × 8 tabs.

**AC2 — production-scale decision point: PASS (documented, with a doc gap).** A 1,200-file corpus was assembled from real MockSite page captures. Running `webminer all` with defaults encoded only 40 files, dropped 1,160, and still printed `PIPELINE COMPLETE` — exactly the documented trap — mitigated by a clear stderr warning naming the exact re-run command (`--max-files 1200`). Per SKILL.md §4d and `decision-trees.md`, >1,000 pages maps to the commercial Apache Spark pipeline; the free local SMILE workflow is not the right tool at that scale. Gap: no bundled document says *how* to route a corpus to the commercial deployment (no link, contact, or procedure).
background.executionContext:
Key commands (all via `./b4w.ps1`, run from the repo root, session `-s wm`):

1. `help`, `--help webminer`, `--help webminer all/views`, `--help crawl`, `--help swarm/query/create`, `--help htmlsnapshot`, `--help webdb/export`; read `skills/browser4-cli/SKILL.md` plus `references/decision-trees.md`, `references/webdb.md`, `references/swarm.md`, and the sibling `skills/browser4-web-miner/SKILL.md`. MockSite was already running on 18080 (verified with curl; product IDs discovered from `/ec/sitemap.xml`, 101 products).
2. AC3: `goto` → `htmlsnapshot export --file corpus-small/B0A00xxxx.html` ×3.
3. AC1: `webminer version` (already installed, v0.0.8, Java 17+ auto-detected — no `webminer install` needed); `webminer all <corpus-small>`; verified CSV/kmeans/views; `webminer views <result-dir>`.
4. AC4: seed file (8 URLs) → `crawl --seed-file … --depth 0 --refresh` (8/8) → `webdb export "<comma-urls>" corpus-bulk` (8/8) → `webminer all corpus-bulk` (8 files, 478 nodes).
5. AC5: `swarm create --display-mode HEADLESS`; `swarm query --seed-file … --sql @…/product-query.sql --refresh` (8 jobs), `swarm list`, `swarm result <id>`, `swarm status <batch-id>`; expanded to 24 URLs with `--wait`; then a cached 4-URL batch to isolate the cause of the slow fresh path.
6. AC2: built `corpus-large` (1,200 files from 10 real MockSite templates), `webminer all` with defaults, captured the truncation warning.
7. Reliability investigation: reproducible `PrivacyException` failures → `crawl result --verbose/--json`, backend `pulsar.log` inspection, `MultiPrivacyContextManager.kt` source review, URL-string variants, single-URL isolation, `swarm close` (no effect), `stop` + retry (fixed).

Decisions/workarounds: used a named session (`-s wm`) per the concurrency rule; used `webdb export` (found in the webdb reference, not in §4d) as the documented way to stage crawled HTML for WebMiner; when crawl kept refusing fresh fetches, verified the same pages were still reachable via `goto` + `htmlsnapshot export` (the AC3 path) and used `stop` to recover the backend. All scratch artifacts live in `.test-sessions/20261015T0901431699046Z/` (see `EVALUATION-NOTES.md` there; note the directory already contained leftovers from a previous run of this same scenario, which I did not touch). A leftover note: the run directory's timestamp predates today — I wrote only new files into it.

assessment.completionStatus: Successful - all five acceptance criteria were executed and verified end-to-end against the local MockSite and the locally built backend: AC3 (3 single-page exports), AC1 (free pipeline on the small corpus + views rebuild), AC4 (8-URL seed crawl, 8/8, plus webdb export staging), AC5 (swarm session + seed-file submission, 8/8 and 24/24 completed with correct X-SQL results), AC2 (1,200-page corpus demonstrating the free-tier truncation and the documented commercial Spark decision point). One major reliability incident (fetch-layer PrivacyException wedge) interrupted AC4 mid-session and was recovered by restarting the backend.
assessment.successRate: 95% - every scripted step produced the expected result; the losses were transient failures inside one crawl (13 of 24 pages) before the fetch layer was diagnosed and reset.
assessment.majorBlockers: The fetch layer wedged mid-session: every fresh crawl fetch failed with 'PrivacyException / status 1601' while goto/htmlsnapshot still worked, and no CLI command recovered it - only ./b4w.ps1 stop (full backend restart) restored fetching. A second, related incident: the backend JVM died abruptly during a crawl, surfacing only as 'HTTP request failed: error sending request for url (...)'.
assessment.mostConfusingAspects: 1) Where the WebMiner artifacts actually live - the encoded dataset and the interactive report go to %TEMP%\webminer-pereg\... while --output receives only the clustering results, and the browsable index.html is a directory listing rather than the report (<project>.html). 2) How crawled HTML gets from crawl/swarm into WebMiner - the skill says 'feed the HTML directory in' but never mentions that pages land in webdb and must be staged with webdb export (found only in the webdb reference). 3) The default --max-files 40 truncation that still reports PIPELINE COMPLETE. 4) Why swarm, the documented 'high-throughput' path, is measurably slower than plain crawl for the same URLs, and why its error text ('retry once the browser pool recovers') never comes true without a restart.
assessment.mostValuableImprovements: 1) Make the privacy-context pool self-healing and give the CLI a way to reset it (and surface the condition in doctor/status) - this is the difference between 'flaky' and 'trustworthy' for the bulk-acquisition paths. 2) Put the critical WebMiner caveats (default truncation, temp-dir outputs, <project>.html vs index.html) into `webminer all --help` and print the truncation count in the stdout completion banner. 3) Add the crawl/swarm -> webdb export -> webminer staging recipe to SKILL.md section 4d, plus a concrete pointer for the commercial tier. 4) Fix or soften the swarm 'high throughput' guidance, or fix the serialized fresh-load path that makes it slower than crawl at small scale.

issues.title: Fetch layer wedges: fresh crawl fetches fail with PrivacyException until the backend is restarted

sections.body:
1) ./b4w.ps1 -s wm swarm create --display-mode HEADLESS
2) ./b4w.ps1 -s wm crawl --seed-file seeds/products-24.txt --depth 0 --refresh   -> 'Crawl completed. 24 pages found.' but Summary: ok: 11, failed: 13 (PrivacyException)
3) ./b4w.ps1 -s wm crawl --seed-file seeds/unseen-6.txt --depth 0 --refresh     -> 4 of 6 fail, reproducible across runs
4) ./b4w.ps1 -s wm crawl "http://localhost:18080/ec/dp/B0HLT0001" --depth 0 --refresh  -> a brand-new URL fails alone
5) ./b4w.ps1 -s wm goto "http://localhost:18080/ec/dp/B0HLT0003"  -> still works (session browser is healthy)
6) ./b4w.ps1 swarm close  -> no effect;  ./b4w.ps1 stop  then retry -> fetching works again
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Fresh fetches succeed (all URLs return HTTP 200 and are served by a local mock server), and if the pool is temporarily exhausted the system recovers on its own (the error text says 'retry once the browser pool recovers').
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Every fresh fetch returns status 1601 with 'fetch returned 0 bytes: the fetch layer queued a retry (PrivacyException) - usually the privacy/browser layer refusing the fetch before any network I/O; retry once the browser pool recovers'. The crawl runner retries each page 3 times then marks it failed; the pool never recovered on its own (~6 minutes observed). Cached/store reads keep working, so failures are easily masked. Only a full backend restart (./b4w.ps1 stop + next command) restored fetching - after which all 6 previously-failing URLs returned 200.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: MultiPrivacyContextManager.run() cannot obtain a ready privacy context for FetchTasks (tryGetNextReadyPrivacyContext throws PrivacyException); the log shows repeated 'PrivacyException, retry later (1/5)' while the crawl-level runner gives up after 3 attempts, so pages fail even though the privacy layer's own retry budget is not exhausted. Contexts held by long-lived sessions (the wm session plus a swarm session with 2 browser contexts) appear to exhaust or stall the pool, and nothing replenishes it. The FetchTask.nRetries counter is only incremented inside the PrivacyException branch, so the underlying 'no ready context' condition is never surfaced with its own message. Exact trigger (pool sizing, context retirement, swarm context life-cycle) needs investigation with backend logging at DEBUG for MultiPrivacyContextManager.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-core/browser4-protocol/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/protocol/browser/emulator/context/MultiPrivacyContextManager.kt (run(), tryGetNextReadyPrivacyContext, isPrivacyRetryAllowed); browser4-rest/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/rest/api/service/crawl/CrawlRoundRunner.kt (per-page 3-attempt retry) and CrawlSupport.kt:670 (error text)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Make pool exhaustion self-healing: recreate/retire privacy contexts when none are ready instead of failing tasks, and expose the condition in `doctor status --section browsers`
- Surface the real cause in the CLI error (e.g. 'no ready privacy context; run `browser4-cli stop` to reset the browser pool') instead of only the generic PrivacyException wrapper
- Add a CLI recovery command (reset/recycle the browser pool) so users do not need a full backend restart that also risks in-flight work
- Align the retry budgets: the crawl runner's 3 attempts should not be able to exhaust the privacy layer's 5-attempt budget silently
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Swarm fresh fetches appear serialized - ~3x slower than crawl for the same seed set

sections.body:
SAME 8-URL seed file, fresh pages (--refresh):
  time ./b4w.ps1 -s wm crawl --seed-file seeds/products.txt --depth 0 --refresh        -> ~9.9s, 8/8 ok
  time ./b4w.ps1 swarm query --seed-file seeds/products.txt --sql @product-query.sql --refresh --wait  -> ~26s for 8/8
  ./b4w.ps1 swarm list --limit 8   -> per-task durations ramp 6.9s, 8.3s, 10.9s, 13.5s, 16.0s, 18.6s, 22.7s, 25.3s (~2.6s stagger)
  (same pattern with 24 URLs: 0 failed, 113s, durations ramp 13.7s -> 1m52s)
  Control: ./b4w.ps1 swarm query --seed-file seeds/products-4.txt --sql @product-query.sql --wait -> cached hits complete in 9-13ms each, in parallel
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Per SKILL.md and references/swarm.md, swarm is the high-throughput path: 'Jobs are enqueued and distributed across contexts automatically' / 'parallel execution across multiple browser contexts for high throughput', preferred when acquisition throughput matters more than sequential crawling.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: With a swarm session of 2 contexts x 8 tabs, fresh page loads complete one at a time at a near-constant ~2.5s interval regardless of context/tab budget - i.e. effectively serial. Cached task results are returned in parallel (milliseconds), so the serialization is specific to the fresh-load path. Net effect: for a local/known-URL corpus, crawl (default parallel 4) is ~3-7x faster end-to-end than swarm for the same URLs.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Suspected: the fresh page-load path relies on a shared resource (browser instance / loader / tab pool) that serializes, or per-task context/tab setup dominates; needs measurement of scheduler and context utilisation during a swarm run. Not explained by CLI flags (--max-browser-contexts 2, --max-open-tabs 8 were in effect). A weaker alternative explanation (slow image loads amortised by crawl's parallelism) does not explain the cached-vs-fresh contrast.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-rest swarm controller / browser driver-pool scheduling (e.g. the SwarmController query path); CLI side: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs (swarm query submission/polling)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Measure and fix the fresh-load path so tasks actually run in parallel across the configured contexts, or document the real throughput characteristics
- Until then, soften the 'high throughput / preferred when acquisition throughput matters' guidance for small single-machine corpora, where `crawl --depth 0 --parallel 8` is measurably faster
- Add a swarm status output that shows per-context utilisation so users can tell whether jobs are running in parallel
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Backend process died mid-crawl and the CLI only reported a raw HTTP transport error

sections.body:
After ./b4w.ps1 stop (which auto-restarts the backend on the next command):
  ./b4w.ps1 -s wm crawl --seed-file seeds/unseen-6.txt --depth 0 --refresh --format table
  -> pages 1..4 of 6 fetched OK, then: 'Error: HTTP request failed: error sending request for url (http://127.0.0.1:8282/api/crawl/b52978ba-.../result)'
  ./b4w.ps1 status -> 'The backend is not running'
  tail of the backend pulsar.log ends abruptly at 02:27:56 with no shutdown lines (log: browser4-apps/browser4-bundle/target/runtime-bundle/_work/.../logs/pulsar.log)
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Either the crawl completes, or the CLI reports that the backend died (and how to recover), rather than a raw client-transport error, leaving the user unable to distinguish a backend death from a network glitch; the interrupted crawl should be resumable via the documented `crawl list`/`crawl resume` path.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The JVM died abruptly mid-crawl with no error in its own log and no hs_err_*.log found; the CLI printed only 'error sending request for url (...)'. A later `crawl list` worked once the backend auto-restarted, but nothing told the user the server had died or that recovery was automatic.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Unknown - needs investigation. Two plausible causes: (a) a JVM/Chrome-driver hard crash (no dump found, so possibly an external kill); (b) a race with the preceding `stop`, whose process-tree cleanup may have killed the backend that the very next command had just auto-started (~10s earlier). Reproduce by running `stop` immediately followed by a long crawl and watching for a second backend death.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs (backend health/error handling for crawl result polling)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Detect 'connection refused/reset' during command polling and print 'the backend appears to have stopped; it will restart on the next command' plus the interrupted task id
- Ensure `stop`'s managed-process cleanup cannot race with an auto-start of a new backend
- Promote the crawl task to 'interrupted' so the documented `crawl resume <id>` path is offered explicitly
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
